questions.stem: In a parallel circuit, what can be said about the potential difference across each branch?

options.text: It is different for each branch
It is the same across each branch
It is zero across all branches
It depends on the wire length

questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit, the potential difference across each branch is the same and equals the supply voltage. This is because each branch is directly connected to the same two points in the circuit.

questions.stem: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: Using 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2 = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2. Therefore R_total = 2 Ω. The total resistance in parallel is always less than the smallest individual resistance.
